content_preview.summary: Qt 6.12, released September 30 as a five-year Long-Term Support version, adds native QML hot reload, a production-ready CanvasPainter API and HarmonyOS as an LTS platform.
content_preview.body_excerpt:
## Overview

The Qt Company published Qt 6.12 on September 30, 2026. According to the [Qt blog](https://www.qt.io/blog/qt-6.12-released), the release is a Long-Term Support (LTS) version, which the post describes as one that "gets maintenance over a 5-year period." The headline changes for developers are native hot reload in the QML engine and a CanvasPainter drawing API that has moved out of preview.

editor_notes.content_quality: Briefing of 535 words (range 300-800) with Overview, What We Know, What We Don't Know and Analysis. Clear, well organized, appropriate depth. Direct quotes are limited and verbatim.
editor_notes.source_verification: Read both snapshots from disk (gunzip). source-0.html.gz (qt.io/blog/qt-6.12-released, HTTP 200, Volker Hilsheimer, Sep 30, 2026): confirms LTS 'gets maintenance over a 5-year period' (verbatim) and the 'Long-Term Support with 5 Years of Maintenance' section; QML Engine 'has been extended to enable native support of the hot reload mechanism, and the qmlpreview tool has been reworked to use it' (verbatim, qmlpreview is code-formatted in the source); CanvasPainter 'imperative painter-like rendering API for C++ and QML that uses the GPU for hardware acceleration, and that can use shaders' and 'ready for production for both C++ and QML developers' (core API out of Technology Preview); Canvas2D 'is modelled after the HTML Canvas, and makes it easy to use JavaScript to draw shapes' (verbatim) and remains in technology preview; StyleKit 'provides a QML-based styling API that lets you style both Widgets and Qt Quick from a single source' (verbatim) BUT the same section is headed 'StyleKit Is Available in Labs: Try It Out' and the summary says 'a new StyleKit in Labs'; QRangeModel built-in sorting 'allows the model to sort its data directly'; QtGrpc client-side compression with selectable algorithms; HarmonyOS 'Starting with Qt 6.12, Qt officially supports HarmonyOS as a Long-Term Support (LTS) platform' (verbatim); CRA sentence 'Qt 6.12 is built to meet the requirements set by the CRA as we today know will take effect in December 2027' (verbatim), within a section stating 'The commercial Qt 6.12 LTS is compliant with the EU Cyber Resilience Act (CRA)'. source-1.html.gz (linuxiac.com, Bobby Borisov, Sep 30, 2026, HTTP 200): confirms five-year maintenance, built-in Hot Reload in the QML Engine ('available through Qt Creator and the command line using the qmlpreview tool' verbatim; 'see changes to a running QML interface as they edit the code without restarting the application'), CanvasPainter Technology Preview in Qt 6.11 and production-ready core API for C++ and QML, Canvas2D remains in Technology Preview, Qt Graphs logarithmic axes/axis-label customization/zoom and pan, QtQuick.Controls.Native, Qt Quick 3D Physics joint types, WebAssembly audio/video, resource deduplication, HarmonyOS 'officially supported as an LTS platform', and that the commercial edition is prepared for the CRA. Extra-scrutiny items: five-year LTS (confirmed by both sources), native hot reload and CanvasPainter descriptions (confirmed, accurate), HarmonyOS as LTS platform (confirmed verbatim by Qt blog, corroborated by Linuxiac). Vendor-only claims (Qt blog alone, Linuxiac does not corroborate): the verbatim StyleKit quote, the CanvasPainter 'uses shaders' detail, the CRA December 2027 quote, and the 'Canvas2D modelled after the HTML Canvas' quote (Linuxiac paraphrases the last). The article attributes each of these to the Qt blog, so attribution is correct, but readers should know the LTS, HarmonyOS and CRA claims are the vendor's own statements. Everything else is corroborated by the independent outlet, although Linuxiac is itself a summary of the Qt announcement and not independent reporting. Neither snapshot was fetched via WebFetch.
editor_notes.suspicious_patterns: Manifest suspicious_patterns is null for both sources; no injection-like text found.
editor_notes.factual_accuracy: All specifics, dates and quotes trace to the cited snapshots. Two omissions of qualifiers present in the source: (1) StyleKit is a Qt Labs module ('Available in Labs: Try It Out'), not a supported 6.12 module, but the article presents it under 'Styling, models and networking' without that qualifier; (2) the CRA statement is made by Qt about the commercial Qt 6.12 LTS (and Qt says it does not make a product automatically compliant), which the article omits. Neither affects the headline, summary or lead; both are covered by clarifications.
editor_notes.tone_assessment: Neutral and factual; no promotional language beyond quoted vendor text. The Analysis section is restrained and flags that gains are not quantified.
editor_notes.originality: No earlier Qt 6.x release coverage in the archive (grep for Qt/QML finds only Audacity 4.0 on Qt, OpenShot 4.0 Qt6, and incidental mentions). New topic; Audacity 4.0 Qt rewrite article linked as related context.
editor_notes.allowlist: linuxiac.com is on config/source_allowlist.txt. qt.io is NOT on the allowlist (script warning). qt.io is the Qt Company's own release announcement and the primary source for a Qt release, so I treat the allowlist warning as non-substantive and recommend adding qt.io to the allowlist. The warning-driven verdict is retained as APPROVE_WITH_CORRECTIONS because of the clarifications above.
concerns: qt.io not on the source allowlist (primary vendor source, recommend adding).
Core LTS, HarmonyOS and CRA claims rest on the vendor blog alone; Linuxiac largely restates the announcement.
StyleKit presented without its Qt Labs status; CRA compliance statement presented without the commercial-edition qualifier.
recommendations: Carry source-status qualifiers (Labs, technology preview, commercial-only) into the body when summarizing a feature list.
editor_notes.overall_assessment: Accurate, well-sourced, correctly scoped briefing. Publish with a short corrections record clarifying the StyleKit Labs status and the commercial-edition scope of the CRA statement.
